rationale: The plan correctly identifies the fatal limitation of n=1 per group, explicitly refuses any inferential test, produces no p-values or FDR, and names the replication (>=3 per condition) required for inference — exactly what the reference demands. QC is design-aware (library sizes, detection, blind VST, single pairwise distance, noting PCA is degenerate with two samples), the filter (>=10 counts in >=1 sample, justified by smallest group size) is minimal and reasoned, and normalization is median-of-ratios inside the model with no pre-scaling. The main technical error is Step 5: apeglm shrinkage is fitted on a negative-binomial GLM whose dispersions cannot be estimated with one sample per group, so a 'shrunken' log2FC here is not well-founded and quietly reintroduces model machinery the plan just declared invalid; a plain normalized-count log ratio would have been cleaner. The GO ORA step is questionable in warrant — the input list is a non-inferential fold-change ranking — and although it is hedged and specifies the tested-gene universe and org.Hs.eg.db mapping, it omits a GO collection version and any gene-set size window despite the final report claiming one. Reporting is otherwise thorough on design, versions, thresholds, gene counts, and caveats.
